Kuvitus: pöydällä on korkea lasi kylmää: Illustration: a tall glass of a cold drink stands on a table, with ice cubes and a straw floating in it. Water droplets have condensed on the outside of the glass, and a box of ice cubes stands next to the glass.
Pylväskuvaaja mittakaavassa: kolme lämpö: Bar chart drawn to scale: three quantities of heat in kilojoules for the same mixture of water and ice that has been in a freezer. The grid spacing is 5 kJ and the numbers are at every 10 kJ. The top bar, the quantity of heat given out by the water as it cools to 0 °C, ends at 25 kJ. The middle bar, the quantity of heat needed to warm the ice to 0 °C, ends at 5 kJ. The bottom bar, the quantity of heat needed to melt all the ice, ends at 60 kJ.

Kaavakuva ennen ja jälkeen: eristetyssä: Before-and-after schematic: an insulated container first holds 0.30 kg of water at 20 °C and 0.10 kg of ice at 0 °C. Heat Q is transferred from the water to the ice. At equilibrium the thermometer reads 0 °C, there is 0.375 kg of water and only 0.025 kg of ice is left. The total area of the ice cubes is drawn to scale with the mass of the ice.
Energiataseen palkit mittakaavassa, kilo: Energy balance bars drawn to scale, in kilojoules: 0.30 kg of water at 20 °C gives out 25.1 kJ when it cools to 0 °C. 0.10 kg of ice at −10 °C needs 2.1 kJ to warm to 0 °C and 33.4 kJ to melt, 35.5 kJ in total. The heat from the water is not enough: the pale part of the bar shows the ice that does not have time to melt.
